documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Faculty Excellence (CAFE)
documents.title: Faculty Samples (AI in the Classroom)
documents.stance_why: The page offers four sample statements ('not allowed', 'not allowed unless specifically stated as allowed', 'allowed unless specifically stated as not allowed', 'fully allowed with citation') and faculty examples, and sets no rule for the campus; the choice is left to the instructor, so the stance is delegates with tiers.
tiers: Generative AI use not allowed unless specifically stated as allowed
Generative AI use allowed unless specifically stated as not allowed
Generative AI use fully allowed with citation
documents.summary: A CAFE page of resources for faculty: sample syllabus AI statements ranging from a full ban to full permission with citation, one music-industry instructor's detailed policy, a mechanical engineering policy with tiers (linked PDF), and sample AI classroom activities and prompts. It is shared faculty material, not an official campus policy.

units.why: The page says the ME instructor's policy has 'AI policy tiers' referenced in the syllabus; this describes a tiered scheme (details are in a linked PDF not in the text), so it is P05 and informs, not a rule itself.
units.anchor: how the different AI policy tiers are referenced and integrated
units.frag_start: You can also see a sample
units.policy: A Mechanical Engineering instructor's AI policy uses tiers that are referenced in course assessments and activities.

units.why: The syllabus says gen AI is 'permitted' for 'checking grammar and style'. It is a permission on writing-support uses, so P18 (prose) rather than P12.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style

units.why: Brainstorming 'and refining your ideas' is listed as a permitted AI activity; this is idea generation, P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas

units.why: 'Finding information on your topic' is a permitted use, like a search engine for understanding a topic, so P12.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic

units.why: 'Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts' is permitted; it is idea structuring, closest to brainstorming and exploring approaches (P15) rather than prose production.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts

units.why: The use of AI is 'not permitted' for impersonating the student, e.g. composing discussion posts or journal entries assigned to them. It is a ban on AI producing submitted work, so P19 (P58 is about messages to staff, which this is not).
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts

units.why: 'Writing a draft of a writing assignment' is on the not-permitted list; AI may not produce the submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment

units.why: 'Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers' with AI is not permitted; this bars AI-generated submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments

units.why: Students 'are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query', including IP and misinformation; this is ownership of submitted content, P29 (P31 would be about verifying output specifically).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query

units.why: 'must be properly documented and cited' is a disclosure requirement for any AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: 'Use of these tools without disclosure is academically dishonest' makes nondisclosure itself the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Use of these tools without disclosure is academically dishonest

units.why: AI used 'in unauthorized ways will be penalized as a violation of academic integrity', so it is classed as misconduct, P36 (the penalty is not specific enough for P37).
units.anchor: will be penalized as a violation of academic integrity

units.why: The instructor will use 'TurnItIn' on all papers 'routinely', a similarity check used to identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: I will use TurnItIn, Cal Poly Pomona's plagiarism tool, on all papers routinely

units.why: 'I may use AI detection tools as well' states instructor use of detectors to find misuse, P40; it does not say detector output is not relied on, so not P39.
units.anchor: I may use AI detection tools as well

units.why: If reports show 'high probability of AI usage' the instructor will 'ask you to meet with me and explain your work process and product'; this is a meeting to check understanding of the work, P34 (P57 is about talking before escalating, a looser fit).
units.anchor: I will ask you to meet with me and explain your work process and product

units.why: 'cite each usage in each specific section as you proceed' requires marking AI use where it occurs, not just at the end, P27 (prose, but the point is placement).
units.anchor: cite each usage in each specific section as you proceed in your paper

units.why: Students who use AI must 'save your original text PRIOR to using AI'; this is keeping drafts as process evidence, P26.
units.anchor: make sure to save your original text PRIOR to using AI

units.why: The instructor will 'ask me to show me your original (pre-AI) work' when students explain their process; this is submitting drafts on request, P26.
units.anchor: I will ask you to show me your original (pre-AI) work

units.why: Academic dishonesty 'will result in at least a failing grade for that percentage of the class grade', a concrete penalty, P37.
units.anchor: will result in at least a failing grade for that percentage of the class grade

units.why: The first sample says gen AI tools 'are not permitted in this class', a default ban for the whole class, P01.
units.anchor: are not permitted in this class

units.why: 'Work in this class is expected to be entirely the product of your own effort' says submitted work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: expected to be entirely the product of your own effort and learning

units.why: 'failing grade for the assignment, with more severe penalties possible' states a concrete penalty for unauthorized AI, P37.
units.anchor: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in a failing grade

units.why: 'You are expected and encouraged to talk to me if you have any questions' tells students to ask the instructor, P10.
units.anchor: You are expected and encouraged to talk to me

units.why: The second sample says AI 'not allowed in this class unless the specific assignment clearly states' it is allowed, a fallback default, P06 (P04 is per-assignment choice, covered in the next unit).
units.anchor: not allowed in this class unless the specific assignment clearly states

units.why: 'Certain assignments in this course will permit or encourage the use of specific gAI tools' makes the rule vary by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course will permit or encourage

units.why: 'gAI use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' is a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: gAI use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited

units.why: The third sample says gAI 'is allowed in this class with detailed acknowledgement and description of its use', a default permit with conditions, P02.
units.anchor: is allowed in this class with detailed acknowledgement and description

units.why: Allowed 'unless the specific assignment clearly states that gAI use is not allowed' lets individual assignments forbid AI, P04.
units.anchor: unless the specific assignment clearly states that gAI use

units.why: 'ALL gAI use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: ALL gAI use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited

units.why: 'use of unacknowledged AI tools will result in a failing grade' makes failure to disclose the violation, P28 (the penalty is part of the same clause).
units.anchor: The use of unacknowledged AI tools will result in a failing grade

units.why: 'Some assignments in this class will specifically disallow or forbid the use of gAI tools' because the work must be the student's own; per-assignment prohibition, P04.
units.anchor: Some assignments in this class will specifically disallow or forbid

units.why: For assignments that forbid AI, 'unauthorized AI tools will result in a failing grade', a concrete penalty, P37.
units.anchor: For these assignments, the use of unauthorized AI tools will result in a failing grade

units.why: Students are encouraged to talk to the instructor 'if your citations of AI tool use are adequate'; asking before relying on a use, P10.
units.anchor: if your citations of AI tool use are adequate

units.why: The fourth sample says gAI 'is allowed in this class with detailed acknowledgement and description', a permit by default, P02.
units.anchor: is allowed in this class with detailed acknowledgement and description

units.why: 'ALL usage of gAI tools must be disclosed' is a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: ALL usage of gAI tools must be disclosed

units.why: 'The use of undisclosed AI tools will result in a failing grade' makes nondisclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: The use of undisclosed AI tools will result in a failing grade

units.why: The faculty reports class 'consensus' that AI is cheating 'when students use it to replace their own thinking, voice, or effort'; this expresses students staying the primary thinker, P32 (informs, as a sample classroom reflection).
units.anchor: it is cheating when students use it to replace their own thinking, voice, or effort

units.why: Students said AI 'can be like a tutor, explaining or giving examples of concepts, checking their answers'; this describes tutor-like uses, P12, informs because it is reported discussion not a rule.
units.anchor: AI can be like a tutor, explaining or giving examples of concepts
units.frag_start: They explained that AI can be

units.why: The instructor asked the class to discuss when AI is useful or cheating, co-articulating appropriate use with students; no type covers building the policy with students.
units.anchor: Collaborating with students to articulate appropriate use of gAI
units.uncovered_note: Instructor co-develops the course AI-use norms with students through a class discussion activity at the start of term.

units.why: The page aims for samples to 'spark your creativity in weaving generative AI tools into your curriculum', encouraging faculty to explore AI in teaching, P63.
units.anchor: weaving generative AI tools into your curriculum

units.why: The page lists AI prompts for 'assessments, feedback, rubric development' for faculty use in their own teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: including assessments, feedback, rubric development, and beyond

documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Faculty Excellence (CAFE)
documents.title: About Navigating AI in the Classroom at CPP
documents.stance_why: The page says it 'does not represent any official policy' and that 'no official university policy regarding gAI exists yet'; it lists concerns and benefits and offers faculty support, with no rule for students, so it sets no stance.
documents.summary: A short framing page from the faculty teaching center stating that no official AI policy exists, listing teaching concerns (integrity, over-reliance, accuracy and bias) and positive uses, and describing CAFE workshops and consultations for faculty.

units.why: The page says 'no official university policy regarding gAI exists yet' and the guide is not official policy; this states the institution's policy status, which no type covers.
units.anchor: While no official university policy regarding gAI exists yet
units.uncovered_note: Statement that no official university-wide AI policy exists and the guide is not official Academic Senate policy.

units.why: The page names that 'Unapproved use of gAI to complete assignments can compromise learning and constitute plagiarism', classing unapproved AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Unapproved use of gAI to complete assignments can compromise learning and constitute plagiarism

units.why: 'Students may become overly reliant on gAI, hindering their development of critical thinking' says AI use undercuts skill-building practice, P41.
units.anchor: hindering their development of critical thinking and research skills

units.why: 'gAI outputs can be inaccurate or biased, requiring careful evaluation and fact-checking' tells users to verify output, P31 (P53 bias is secondary).
units.anchor: gAI outputs can be inaccurate or biased, requiring careful evaluation and fact-checking

units.why: 'gAI can help students brainstorm ideas, overcome writer's block' names brainstorming as a positive use, P15.
units.anchor: gAI can help students brainstorm ideas, overcome writer's block

units.why: 'gAI can provide personalized support to students, tailoring content and practice to their needs' describes practice and study support, P14.
units.anchor: gAI can provide personalized support to students, tailoring content and practice to their needs

units.why: 'gAI can automate repetitive tasks, freeing up faculty time' describes faculty use of AI for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: gAI can automate repetitive tasks, freeing up faculty time for more in-depth student interaction

units.why: CAFE offers 'Workshops on gAI for Teaching and Learning' so faculty learn tools and strategies, P63.
units.anchor: Workshops on gAI for Teaching and Learning

units.why: CAFE offers 'Guidance on Course Development' on how AI can enhance learning objectives and assessments, supporting faculty before they set policy, P63.
units.anchor: Guidance on Course Development

units.why: 'Individualized Consultations' let faculty develop strategies for gAI use in their courses, P63.
units.anchor: Individualized Consultations

notes: Coded two included CAFE documents. No computing or course-layer documents were screened in. Hassanpour ME policy and Syllabus PDFs and Eaton resources are linked, not in the saved text, so uncoded.
